sent_to_model:
I need to write to Niamh Fahy, who coordinates the volunteers at Corrib Reading Partners. She emailed last week to say our Tuesday reading club at Knocknacarra library is to be 'paused' after Christmas because the numbers were poor. Well, the numbers are not poor any more, and I'm thrilled, and I want her to know it before the review meeting. But I've also gone and done something I shouldn't have, which is tell a reporter from the Corrib Courier she could come and take photographs, and I know full well that has to go through Niamh first. I'd rather she heard it from me. Would you draft the email for me? I don't want to grovel, and I don't want it to read like I'm going over her head either.

- club runs Tuesdays 3.30 to 4.45 in the meeting room upstairs at Knocknacarra library, since September 2025
- Niamh's email of 30 Oct said pause from January, low attendance and the hall insurance going up
- attendance was 5 most weeks in September, 9 by mid-October, 14 children last Tuesday (3 Nov)
- Salthill Book Nook (owner Declan Moran) donated 120 books, mostly 6-9 age group, a good few as Gaeilge
- review meeting is Wednesday 18 November
- reporter is Orla Keane, Corrib Courier (local weekly), wants to come Tuesday 24 Nov with a photographer
- policy says no photos of children without Niamh's sign-off and the parental consent forms
- two sisters from a Ukrainian family started in October, the older one now reads to the younger one in English at the end of each session
- one boy who wouldn't open a book in September asked last week could he take two home
- I met Orla at the farmers' market, got carried away telling her and said 'come along any Tuesday'
- pausing now would be a terrible pity just as it has taken off
- the coverage could be wonderful for us, but only if it's done properly
- I was wrong not to check first, plain and simple
- Niamh to see the new numbers before the 18th and reconsider the pause
- offer to ring Orla and put the visit on hold until Niamh decides
- offer to collect consent forms myself if she says yes
- warm, not defensive
- do not name the Kavanagh boy or mention his family's business, that's private

(About me: retired primary-school teacher, 71, Galway, Ireland. Length: it should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

must_cover: Gives the improved attendance and asks Niamh to reconsider the pause before the review meeting.
Discloses the unapproved reporter invitation and accepts responsibility.
Offers to hold the visit pending approval and collect parental consent forms if approved.

reference.kind: a model-written solution, used only to show the checks can be met
